correctness.rationale: Reconstructed finite abelian unit-group Frattini lifting: for odd p, reduction modulo p² from p^e (e>=3) has kernel in the p-th-power component, hence in Phi; for p=2 reduction modulo 8 from 2^e (e>=4) has kernel in the square subgroup. Cartesian products preserve the Frattini kernel inclusion. As n and kappa(n) have the same prime support, the same admissible initial generators appear, proving G(n)=G(kappa(n)) for all n, with G(1)=G(2)=1. Independently recomputed all 36 reduced {2,3,5} moduli using direct modular subgroup breadth-first closure and verified each claimed B generates, B-1 does not. This proves the four-by-four table and maximum 17 for every exponent triple, not merely a finite-range conjecture. Edge examples G(4)=3, G(8)=5, G(42)=11, G(126)=13 independently checked.
